biography: Jeremy Bentham was an English legal and political reformer who gave utilitarianism one of its first systematic modern forms. He proposed that laws and policies should be judged by their effects on pleasure, pain, and the interests of those affected, rather than by inherited rank or unexamined custom. Bentham used that standard to criticize punishment, legal procedure, and political exclusion. His felicific calculus asks decision-makers to attend to intensity, duration, probability, downstream effects, and the number of people affected. In an AI-policy case, his approach turns a vague claim about efficiency into a disciplined question about whose welfare improves, whose risks are shifted, and what evidence supports the comparison.

teaching.whyThisPerson: Bentham gives students a way to map consequences and test welfare claims in institutional AI decisions.
